claims.text: FeNiCrMn is a high-entropy alloy without the expensive Co component.
The as-prepared FeNiCrMn alloy has a complex, multiphase microstructure.
The FeNiCrMn alloy contains localized phase variations.
Grid-mapping nanoindentation can be applied as an array of 100 indentations over a 100 µm × 100 µm area.
The proposed nanoindentation protocol uses a constant loading rate of 0.05 mN/s and a 10-second dwell at peak load.
The relevant localized microstructural features include phase boundaries.
The relevant localized microstructural features include elemental segregation.
The relevant localized microstructural features include varying crystallographic orientations.
Localized nanoindentation measurements capture variations in hardness and elastic modulus associated with underlying microstructural inhomogeneities.
Macroscopic mechanical tests average out spatial variations in local mechanical properties.
Grid-mapping nanoindentation will reveal a measurable spread in hardness across the mapped area.
Grid-mapping nanoindentation will reveal a measurable spread in elastic modulus across the mapped area.
Regions corresponding to phases with greater stiffness or strength will exhibit higher measured hardness or elastic modulus.
An indent spacing of approximately 10 µm or less is sufficient to resolve the relevant microstructural features.
Highly homogeneous regions may show minimal differences in local hardness and elastic modulus.
